title: HCI — Ergonomics & Musculoskeletal Disorders (story explainer)
description: Exam revision told as a story: meaning of ergonomics, risk factors, six musculoskeletal disorders (carpal tunnel, tendonitis, rotator cuff, epicondylitis, trigger finger, lower back), their effects, prevention, OSHA protections and ergonomics plans.

scenes.title: Intro

viz.s: Why does your body hurt after a long day at the computer?

lines: Meet Arjun, a programmer. Ten hours a day at the keyboard, hunched over a laptop on the sofa.
One month later, his wrist tingles, his back aches, and one finger keeps getting stuck.
This video is about ergonomics: why that happens, and how to stop it.

scenes.title: 1. What you need to know

items.b: carpal tunnel · tendonitis · rotator cuff · epicondylitis · trigger finger · strains & lower back

lines: Here's the checklist. Understand the meaning of ergonomics, and know the basic musculoskeletal disorders, called M S Ds.
Know how preventable M S Ds hurt worker productivity, and how ergonomics prevents them.
Know the regulations and protections for workers, and how to develop a prevention plan.

scenes.title: 2. What is ergonomics? + risk factors

items.b: fitting the person to the job — matching work, tools and environment to the human body
same motion, again and again — typing, clicking

lines: Ergonomics means fitting the person to the job, making the work, the tools and the environment suit the human body.
There are four big risk factors. Lifting heavy items, which means pushing and pulling heavy loads.
Bending and reaching, putting the body in awkward positions.
Performing tasks repetitively. For Arjun, that's thousands of keystrokes and clicks.
And body position, like his slouch on the sofa, held for hours.

scenes.title: 3. MSDs — wrist, tendons, shoulder

parts.b:
• numbness & tingling in the hand
• caused by a pinched nerve in the wrist
• very common: > 3 million US cases a year
• many causes — common in many jobs, including computer work
• very preventable and easily treatable (even surgery)

• inflammation of tendons (microscopic tears)
• caused by overuse (too often) and overload (too much)
• lasts a few days or weeks; risk of re-injury
• treatment: NSAIDs, ice packs, splinting

• a form of tendonitis in the shoulder joint
• not typically common as a computer injury
• symptoms & treatment same as tendonitis

lines: Arjun's wrist tingles. That's carpal tunnel syndrome: numbness and tingling in the hand, caused by a pinched nerve in the wrist.
It's very common, more than three million US cases a year, with many causes, including computer work. Good news: it's very preventable and easily treatable, even with surgery.
Next, tendonitis: inflammation of tendons, from microscopic tears. It's caused by overuse, doing it too often, and overload, doing too much.
It can last days or weeks, with a risk of re-injury. Treatment is anti-inflammatory painkillers called N SAIDs, ice packs, and splinting.
Rotator cuff injury is tendonitis in the shoulder joint. It's not very common as a computer injury, and its symptoms and treatment are the same as tendonitis.

scenes.title: 4. MSDs — elbow, finger, back

parts.b:
• tennis elbow (lateral) · golfer's elbow (medial)
• pain & irritation in the forearm
• very common — racquet sports are a risk factor
• a form of tendonitis; similar treatment

• tenosynovitis — finger gets stuck in a bent position
• inflammation narrows the sheath around finger tendons
• caused mainly by repetitive gripping
• treatment: rest, splint, NSAIDs

• very common in computer & office workers
• correct ergonomic chair heights
• use lower-back supports
• regular posture checks, breaks, exercise, stretching, movement
• true for driving too

lines: Epicondylitis is commonly called tennis elbow, on the outer side, or golfer's elbow, on the inner side. Pain and irritation in the forearm.
It's very common, racquet sports are a risk factor, and it's a form of tendonitis with similar treatment.
Remember Arjun's stuck finger? That's trigger finger, or tenosynovitis. Inflammation narrows the sheath around the finger tendons, so the finger gets stuck bent.
It's caused mainly by repetitive gripping. Treatment: rest, a splint, and N SAIDs.
Finally, lower back pain, very common in computer and office workers. Fix it with correct chair heights, lower back supports,
and regular posture checks, breaks, exercises, stretching and movement. The same applies to driving.

scenes.title: 5. Effects of MSDs

items.b: of all worker injury and illness cases are MSDs (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
most frequently reported cause of lost or restricted work time

lines: Why should employers care? M S Ds account for thirty three percent, one third, of all worker injury and illness cases, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
They're the most frequently reported cause of lost or restricted work time.
And they're strongly linked to quality of life. Arjun can't even hold his phone comfortably.

scenes.title: 6. Prevention

nodes.b: every desk position follows ergonomic guidelines (chair height, screen, keyboard)

lines: Prevention has three parts. First, make sure every desk position follows ergonomic guidelines. Arjun moves from the sofa to a proper chair and desk.
Second, take frequent breaks and do exercises.
Third, recognise the early signs of repetitive task injuries or tendonitis, before they get serious.

scenes.title: 7. OSHA protections

nodes.b: employers must keep the workplace free from recognised serious hazards — including ergonomic hazards

nodes.h: Is it causing, or likely to cause, serious physical harm?
Is there a feasible way to reduce it?

lines: What protects workers by law? In the US, OSHA's General Duty Clause: employers must keep the workplace free from recognised serious hazards, including ergonomic hazards.
To decide whether to cite an employer, OSHA asks four questions. Does an ergonomic hazard exist? Is the hazard recognised?
Is it causing, or likely to cause, serious physical harm to employees? And is there a feasible way to reduce it?
Memory hook: exists, recognised, harmful, fixable.

scenes.title: 8. An ergonomics plan

items.b: management must back the ergonomic process
workplace assessment · identify risks · responsible for avoiding risk factors
a way to report symptoms & hazards

lines: Finally, an ergonomics plan. Management must support the ergonomic process.
Workers must be involved: assessing the workplace, identifying risks, and taking responsibility for avoiding risk factors.
Provide training on ergonomics and risk factors, and have a reporting mechanism,
and an evaluation process to check it's working. Arjun's company now does all five, and his wrist has stopped tingling.

scenes.title: Recap

viz.s: Fit person and job together — before the body breaks

lines: Quick recap.
Four risk factors: lifting, bending, repetition and posture. Six disorders: carpal tunnel, tendonitis, rotator cuff, tennis elbow, trigger finger, and lower back pain.
M S Ds are a third of all injuries. Prevent them with good desks, breaks and early signs, backed by OSHA and a solid plan. You've got this.
